text:
maria: Ran a small experiment to reuse KV cache across sessions by keying on prefix hash + model variant instead of full session id. baseline (sticky-by-session) used ~18GB after 6h; new prefix-keying stabilizes around 12GB but we see higher eviction churn when many short-lived sessions hit the same prefix. sharing traces and quick notes.

alex: can you paste the key function you tried?

maria: sure — the gist: 
```python
def kv_key(model, prefix_tokens, session_id=None, sticky=False):
    prefix_fprint = xxhash64(prefix_tokens)
    base = f"{model}:{prefix_fprint}"
    if sticky and session_id:
        return base + ":" + session_id[:8]  # optional stickiness
    return base
```
we flipped on sticky=False for 80% of traffic in the experiment.

jin: what eviction policy + TTL did you run with? and are you chunking long contexts?

maria: eviction=LFRU (we've been using LFRU for KV), no per-key TTL (relying on max_entries=200k for the shard). long contexts get chunked into 1k-token kv blocks.

priya: interesting. not using session id smells like better reuse but also more cross-tenant collisions if prompt templates are similar. did you include prompt-template id anywhere?

maria: not in this run. it was strictly model + prefix_fprint. collisions observed when templated system prompts are identical across tenants.

perf-bot: [metric] /dash/kv/experiments/1769801234 — eviction_rate: baseline=0.8/s, new=2.6/s during peak; mem_total baseline=18GB, new=12GB steady; tail_lat_p95 increased 30ms on new.

alex: that eviction spike explains the tail increase. maybe we can make the key = model + template_id + prefix_fprint ? that would reduce tenant collisions but still allow reuse across sessions with same template.

jin: also consider stratified caches: hot prefixes in a small sticky cache keyed with session id, cold prefixes in a shared prefix cache. that way hot conversational sessions don't thrash shared slots.

priya: +1. Another thought: keep a short sticky window (e.g., 5 minutes) tied to session id — if session keeps requesting same prefix inside window, we keep a session-specific entry. after window expires fallback to prefix-key only. reduces fragmentation from ephemeral stickiness.

maria: that matches what I was thinking. implementation note: we need a fast fingerprint for long prefixes and a compact key format to avoid key object bloat. also compaction pass for shards to defragment evicted slab segments showed promise in microbenchmarks.

jin: how about doing an AB test: 10% traffic with template+prefix_fprint + short sticky window; compare mem, eviction churn, p95.

maria: will set up. I'll add experiment config to the RFC and schedule a short perf run tomorrow. thanks for the ideas.

alex: small nit — make sure quantized models include model-variant in the key (q4_0 vs q8), otherwise different kernel paths will collide and cause wrong cache hits.

maria: good catch, will add variant. I'll post the RFC link once it's up.

priya: fwiw, we should also log cache hit metadata (prefix_len, session_delta, template_id) to help offline analysis — low overhead counters.

maria: agreed. adding lightweight counters and a sample tracer span for misses. sync tomorrow 10:30.
